bscan_site_decides.why_it_looked_true: across the five W977 seeds the partition was perfect: PASS at BSCAN3 (seeds 1, 42, 31337), FAIL at BSCAN1 (seed 7) and BSCAN2 (seed 1234). 5 of 5.
bscan_site_decides.test: hold the seed, perturb the design so the placer lands the cell elsewhere
bscan_site_decides.result: REFUTED by three of the six new reads: FAIL at BSCAN3 (rows 4, 5), PASS at BSCAN1 (row 7), PASS at BSCAN2 (rows 6, 9)
bscan_site_decides.lesson: the site moved together with the placement, so it could not be separated from it by the sweep that suggested it

timing.test: halve the physical clock at a FIXED BSCAN site -- rows 4 and 5 are the same seed, the same site, and differ only in slowclk (cfgmclk/8 vs cfgmclk/16)
timing.significance: every previous timing argument on this bench rested on nextpnr's own model (W977: the failing seeds hold the BETTER reported margin). This is the first test that changed the physical period instead of reading the model, and the failure did not move.

fmax_predicts.result: the ranges interleave completely; reported Fmax carries no signal about the verdict

netlist_perturbation.observation: seed 1234 FAILED in W977 with a 3-bit divider counter and PASSES here with a 5-bit one at the same divider ratio (row 7)
netlist_perturbation.significance: two bits of a counter that cannot reach the arithmetic flip the verdict -- T614 (W841), now on a second design

fasm_diff_is_not_decisive.w977_plan: the two FASM files (passing seed vs failing seed) have not been diffed, so the specific net that routes differently is unidentified. That diff is the next step.
fasm_diff_is_not_decisive.why_it_fails: the multiset of logic LUT INIT words differs between seed 42 and seed 1 -- TWO BUILDS THAT BOTH COMPUTE THE RIGHT ANSWER (+508 / -509). Pin permutation rewrites INIT bits without changing the function, and nextpnr inserts route-through LUTs freely, so INIT equality is not a function-preservation invariant and inequality is not evidence of a logic change.
fasm_diff_is_not_decisive.consequence: W977's named next step cannot decide the question it was chosen for. A decision needs a formal equivalence check between the pre- and post-place-and-route netlists, not a textual diff of configuration bits.

what_survives: seed 7 is the only persistent failure: 2 reads in W977 and 3 today, across a bench change, a netlist perturbation and a 2x clock slowdown. Its cause is below the front end and is not the placer seed, the BSCAN site, the reported Fmax or the clock period.
